pipeline_name: Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America System

validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, major, active FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural gas transmission system. Confirmed via Kinder Morgan's own current (2026) operations page (Operations/Natural-Gas/Index), which describes NGPL as 'the largest transporter of natural gas into the high-demand Chicago-area market as well as one of the largest interstate pipeline systems in the country,' plus current-vintage FERC activity: a January 2025 FERC order authorizing NGPL's $72M Texas-Louisiana Expansion Project (PGJ + OGJ, both independently reporting the same docket) and Kinder Morgan, Inc.'s own FY2025 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2026-02-13), which lists 'NGPL' as a live equity-method investment with FY2025 miles/capacity/storage figures. Correctly classified Gas/transmission (not gathering/distribution/storage-only) -- every source describes long-haul interstate transportation to Chicago and Gulf Coast LNG/power markets. DUPLICATE CHECK: cross-checked against the full 46-row west-operating roster (Alliance, BC/Westcoast, Bison, Cheyenne Plains, CIG, Great Lakes, Kern River, TIGT, Mojave, North Baja/NBXP, GTN, Panhandle Eastern, REX/REX Cheyenne Hub, Ruby, Southern Trails, Trailblazer, TransColorado, Transwestern, Tuscarora, Viking, Williston Basin, WIC, Northern Border, Line 1600, Norte Crossing, North Mist, Sierrita, Santa Fe Mainline, El Paso/Carlsbad South, North Bakken Expansion, etc.) -- no overlap found. P0222's Texas Permian Basin/Gulf of Mexico-to-Chicago/Illinois corridor and its unique ~9,100-mile multi-lateral scale do not match any other roster row's geography or identity; no duplicate/relabeling risk identified. CAVEAT: this is a SYSTEM-level GEM row (segment_name blank) aggregating a large multi-lateral, multi-vintage network (original 1930-31 mainline + numerous later laterals/expansions, most recently the 2025 Texas-Louisiana Expansion's 30-inch Louisiana Line). Several recorded spec fields (Capacity, Diameter) likely reflect different vintages/scopes of this evolving system rather than a single current uniform value -- flagged separately below where material.

validity.recommendation: Update the operators_owners tab Owner row: Owner1 'Kinder Morgan' stays at 37.50%; Owner2 'Brookfield Infrastructure Partners' 25.00% is STALE and should be removed (or set to 0.00%) -- Brookfield fully exited NGPL; Owner3 'ArcLight Capital Partners' should be updated from 37.50% to 62.50%.
validity.researcher_notes: This is exactly the batch-flagged lead: P0222's ownership row (Kinder Morgan 37.5%; Brookfield 25%; ArcLight 37.5%) matches the June 2023 PRNewswire release EXACTLY -- but NGPL Holdings' cap table changed again after that. On 2025-03-21, Brookfield Infrastructure Partners L.P. signed an agreement to sell its ENTIRE remaining 25% stake in NGPL Holdings LLC to ArcLight Capital Partners (announced via PGJ, 2025-03-xx: 'Brookfield to Sell Pipeline Stake to ArcLight as Part of $1.7 Billion Exit,' explicitly stating the resulting split as Kinder Morgan 37.5% / ArcLight 62.5%). Independent trade-press search (Hart Energy, 'ArcLight Closes $1.7B Deal with Brookfield for NGPL Interests') reports the deal CLOSED 2025-05-13 -- Hart Energy's own site 403-blocks automated fetches (bot-wall, not evidence of deletion; not cited as a proposed_ref for that reason) but the closing is independently corroborated by: (1) Kinder Morgan's OWN CURRENT (2026) operations page, which now states 'NGPL is owned in part by Kinder Morgan, Inc. and funds managed by ArcLight Capital Partners, LLC' -- Brookfield is no longer named as an owner at all on the operator's current site; and (2) Kinder Morgan, Inc.'s own FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-02-13, SEC EDGAR), whose equity-investments table still lists KMI's own NGPL interest at exactly 37.5% -- consistent with KM's stake being unaffected by a Brookfield-to-ArcLight transfer of the OTHER 25% (this does not by itself prove ArcLight now holds 62.5% rather than some other allocation, but it rules out any change to Kinder Morgan's share, and combined with the KM.com page no longer naming Brookfield, and the PGJ announcement's explicit 62.5%/37.5% split, the finding is corroborated by three independent origins: operator's own current site, KMI's own audited 10-K, and contemporaneous trade press). NOTE: even Wikipedia's live article (fetched today, 2026-09-09) is ALSO stale here -- its infobox/lead still says NGPL 'is owned by Kinder Morgan, Brookfield Infrastructure Partners, and ArcLight Capital Partners,' unrevised since the 2023 transaction -- so this is not merely a case of GEM lagging one better-informed secondary source; the correction requires going to the operator's own primary disclosure. A three-way ownership row with stale percentages, exactly the pattern this batch was told to expect.

validity.recommendation: Capacity is very likely stale/wrong. GEM records Capacity=1600.00 MMcf/d; Kinder Morgan, Inc.'s own FY2025 10-K discloses NGPL's total system 'Design (Bcf/d)' capacity as 8.40 Bcf/d (=8,400 MMcf/d), more than 5x the recorded value. Recommend updating Capacity to 8400.00 MMcf/d, pending a second fully independent corroborating figure (see notes -- a directionally consistent but unciteable low-quality source and an inconclusive EIA search were the only additional checks completed).
validity.researcher_notes: KMI's FY2025 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2026-02-13) carries a disclosure table for KMI's equity-method pipeline investments: 'Asset | Ownership Interest | Miles of Pipeline | Design (Bcf/d) Capacity | Storage (Bcf) ... NGPL 37.5% 9,105 8.40 288'. The 9,105-mile and 288-Bcf-storage figures in the SAME row exactly match NGPL's known FULL system totals (not a 37.5% pro-rata slice -- e.g. KM's own site independently states NGPL's storage as 288 Bcf, matching this row precisely), which confirms the '8.40' Design (Bcf/d) figure is also NGPL's own total system design capacity, not a KMI-share-adjusted number: 8.40 Bcf/d = 8,400 MMcf/d. This is materially larger than GEM's recorded 1,600 MMcf/d (1.6 Bcf/d). Searched for a second fully independent source: EIA's public pipeline-capacity releases/today-in-energy pieces did not surface a company-specific NGPL design-capacity figure in the time available. A low-quality, unbylined, internally self-contradictory content-farm page (bluegasexpress.com) states both '6.5 Bcf peak day' (in a table) and '7.8 Bcf/d' (in prose) elsewhere -- excluded as a citable source (fails the source-quality bar; flagged in a prior pass of this research), but its order-of-magnitude (several Bcf/d, not 1.6) is at least directionally consistent with the 10-K figure being closer to correct than GEM's recorded value. Given this is a single verifiable primary-source figure (KMI's own audited 10-K) without a second independent corroboration located, staged as a CONCERN with tier=medium rather than a high-confidence fill -- Update leg should look for an EIA Form-567/pipeline-capacity-report figure or a FERC Form 2 filing for NGPL PipeCo LLC to close the second-source gap before applying.

validity.recommendation: Keep Diameter=24in (matches the pipeline's original 1930-31 construction spec, well-sourced), but flag that the current multi-lateral SYSTEM includes at least one other diameter -- no value change proposed.
validity.researcher_notes: 24-inch is confirmed as NGPL's ORIGINAL construction diameter: Continental Construction (NGPL's predecessor) was incorporated 'for the purpose of constructing a 24-inch natural gas pipeline between the Amarillo, Texas, oil fields and Chicago, Illinois' (Wikipedia, sourced to period newspapers). However, the modern system is multi-lateral and includes other diameters -- e.g. the January-2025 FERC-approved Texas-Louisiana Expansion Project uses NGPL's existing 'Louisiana Line, a system of 30-inch pipelines running from Montgomery County, Texas, to Vermilion Parish, Louisiana' (PGJ and OGJ, independently). Since this is a SYSTEM-level row (no segment breakout), a single Diameter value necessarily oversimplifies a system that has grown to include at least 24-inch and 30-inch mainline/lateral pipe. Not proposing a value change (24in remains defensible as the original/primary mainline spec and is the only diameter with a clean single-value citation), but flagging the caveat for anyone doing route/segment -level work on this system.
